name: Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.
moat_justification: Scale leader in preclinical safety assessment with an integrated NHP supply chain and real switching friction, but returns were only modest even in good years (roic_proxy ~8.5-11.4% FY16-23, ~0% in impairment-hit FY25) and demand is hostage to the biotech funding cycle — a moderate, cyclical moat, not a wide one.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 2.0% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 6.6x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Real CRO franchise, moat 5/10, but at $300.15 the price already pays for a full recovery and more — TTM OE/share of $5.93 supports only a 4.6% weighted IRR (weighted IV@15% $48.96); the shares would need to fall to ~$49 to clear the 15% hurdle.
moat_for: Largest preclinical CRO: scale and capacity in Discovery & Safety Assessment sponsors cannot easily replicate
Integrated nonhuman-primate supply chain — a scarce, hard-to-copy input
Switching friction: safety studies sit on clients' regulatory critical path; track record matters
Research Models installed base and recurring services revenue
moat_against: Demand is cyclical — biotech funding downturn cut revenue and OE for three straight years
ROIC only ~9-11% even in good years; ~0% in FY2025 after impairments — no wide-moat return profile
Non-animal methods (NAMs) and regulatory drift threaten the animal-testing core long-term
Net debt 6.6x normalized OE limits flexibility through the trough
Chinese CRO price competition and large-pharma insourcing
